h1: Most businesses can’t tell what’s holding revenue back, because **every department tracks its own numbers in its own dashboard**.
sub: Even in a one-person business, you’re switching between separate dashboards without seeing how one number moves another.
rooms_h: Everyone who touches revenue, for example
d_ads_r: Brings paid visitors to the site
others: …and everyone else who touches revenue, each watching its own numbers too.
stuck: Every department is succeeding with its own numbers. So why has revenue barely moved?
north_h: Revenue Per Visitor™ becomes your North Star
north_s: It’s the one number every department shares, so each team can see how its work connects to, and influences, everyone else’s success. Here’s what that conversation sounds like:
c1: Our ads hit a 6× ROAS this month. Let’s double down on them.
c2: But 2,499 of every 2,500 visitors from those ads are leaving without opting in or buying.
c3: And our acquisition costs went up. Let’s figure out a way to bring them down.
c4: Don’t. Those customers ask for far fewer refunds, so they’re worth more to us.
plot_h: So everyone who touches revenue plots the same five metrics
five_h: The five metrics that make up Revenue Per Visitor™:
c5: So the ads are working. Opt-ins are the gap. Instead of sending ads straight to the product page, let’s send them to a landing page where buyers give their email.
c6: We’ll build that page with you.
dec_h: The decision: no guesswork, just data
dec: Ads and CRO work on email opt-ins together. Through the Revenue Per Visitor™ lens, raising opt-ins by 20% alone should add **$70,000 to MRR next month**.
ex: Department numbers, the conversation and the five-metric plot are examples. The 6× ROAS story is from a real client project.
cta: Show me my Revenue Per Visitor™ and my five metrics
up_next: Next question: What’s your (and your team’s) biggest challenge right now?
